# Task: Support property-to-property comparisons in Cypher WHERE clauses

## Problem

The Cypher query subset supported by `src/cypher/cypher.c` fails to parse a WHERE condition that compares one variable's property with another variable's property. The query aborts with `expected value at pos N` at the right-hand operand.

Examples that fail on the current code:

```
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.name <> b.name RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name
```

Property-to-literal comparisons already work and must keep working:

```
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE b.file_path = 'demo.go' RETURN a.name, b.name
```

## Required behavior

Extend the WHERE parser and evaluator so that when the right-hand side of a comparison operator is another `variable.property` expression (not a string/number/boolean literal), the condition compares the two resolved property values for the current binding.

1. `a.prop = b.prop` — true when the two resolved string values are equal.
2. `a.prop <> b.prop` — true when the two resolved string values differ.
3. All existing comparison operators that make sense on property values (`>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`) should also accept a property right-hand side, evaluated the same way as when the right-hand side is a numeric literal (via `strtod`).
4. The property right-hand side must resolve through the same binding mechanism used for the left-hand side (`node_prop` / bare-alias name), so File, Function, and other node property paths all work.
5. Property-to-literal and bare-alias comparisons must continue to work exactly as before.
6. The change must work in both the early WHERE (after MATCH) and post-WITH WHERE paths, since they share the same parser and evaluator.

## Where to change

- Parser: `parse_condition_expr` in `src/cypher/cypher.c` currently rejects a non-literal right-hand side with `expected value at pos %d`.
- Condition model: `cbm_condition_t` in `src/cypher/cypher.h` currently only stores a literal `value`.
- Evaluator: `eval_condition` / `resolve_condition_value` in `src/cypher/cypher.c` currently resolve only the left-hand side against the binding.

## Constraints

- Do not break any existing Cypher behavior (WHERE with literals, regex, CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, HAS_LABEL, EXISTS, AND/OR/XOR/NOT).
- Keep the error path for genuinely unsupported right-hand sides (e.g. function calls on the RHS if not already supported) clear and non-crashing.
- Add unit tests in the existing Cypher test suite covering property-to-property `=`, `<>`, and at least one ordering operator, plus a WITH-path case.
- The full project test suite (`make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= test`) must still pass.

## How to verify

```sh
make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= cbm
./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli index_repository '{"repo_path":"/tmp/demo","mode":"full","name":"demo"}'
./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli query_graph '{"project":"demo","query":"MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name"}'
```

Before the fix this errors with `expected value at pos N`. After the fix it returns only CALLS edges whose source and target files are the same.

activities.objective:
Extend the Cypher WHERE parser/evaluator in src/cypher/cypher.c and src/cypher/cypher.h to support property-to-property comparisons (e.g. `WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path`, `WHERE a.name <> b.name`), in both the early-WHERE and post-WITH WHERE paths (they share the same parser/evaluator).

1) Condition model (src/cypher/cypher.h, cbm_condition_t ~line 185): add owned heap fields `const char *rhs_variable; const char *rhs_property;` for a right-hand `variable.property` operand (both NULL when the RHS is a literal). Extend the doc comment on `op` to note that `=`, `<>`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` accept a property RHS.

2) Parser (parse_condition_expr, cypher.c:1009): in the 'Value' section (~lines 1080-1095), before the `expected value at pos` error, accept a token sequence IDENT '.' IDENT: store `c.rhs_variable = heap_strdup(ident->text)` and `c.rhs_property = heap_strdup(prop->text)`. Keep literals (STRING/NUMBER/TRUE/FALSE) working exactly as before; keep the existing error path (with safe_str_free of variable/property/op, plus the new rhs fields) for anything else (e.g. function calls on the RHS). Do NOT allow bare-alias RHS (a variable without a dot) — leave that on the error path.

3) Free path (expr/condition free ~cypher.c:753-756 and any other place that frees cond fields, e.g. parse_in_list error paths): free rhs_variable and rhs_property alongside the existing fields to keep SANITIZE clean.

4) Evaluator (cypher.c ~2331-2466): in eval_condition, after computing `actual` via resolve_condition_value, when c->rhs_variable is set, resolve the RHS value with the same mechanism: check binding_get_edge(b, rhs_variable) first (edge_prop), else binding_get + node_prop(n, rhs_property, b->store) (mirror resolve_condition_value; you may factor a small helper taking (variable, property, binding)). Treat a NULL resolved RHS as "" (empty string) so comparisons don't crash. Then pass the resolved RHS string to eval_comparison_op as `expected` (replacing c->value) so `=`, `<>` (strcmp) and `>`,`<`,`>=`,`<=` (strtod) work identically to the literal case. All special ops (IS NULL, IN, EXISTS, HAS_LABEL, regex, CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH) keep using c->value unchanged.

5) Tests (tests/test_cypher.c, follow existing ASSERT/CBM_TEST style): add cases covering: (a) parse+eval `a.prop = b.prop` returning only same-file CALLS edges; (b) `a.name <> b.name`; (c) one ordering op with property RHS (e.g. `a.line > b.line` or similar available on the test store); (d) a WITH-path case: `MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name`; (e) regression: property-to-literal (`b.file_path = 'demo.go'` or test-store equivalent) still parses and filters as before. Build a small in-memory store like neighboring tests do.

6) Verify: run `make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= test` (full suite must pass, no leaks) and `make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= cbm`. If the CLI demo is feasible, also run the query in the task's How-to-verify section.

Constraints: no behavior change for existing ops; keep unsupported-RHS error clear and non-crashing; minimal diff following existing code style (heap_strdup/safe_str_free).
